html:
A law of 212 by the emperor Caracalla that made almost every free person in the Roman Empire a Roman citizen. Before it, full citizenship was held mainly by people in Italy, Roman colonies and some favoured towns and families.

The historian Cassius Dio said the real aim was money: some taxes, such as the tax on inheritances, fell only on citizens. Caracalla himself presented it as a thank offering to the gods. Part of the text survives on a papyrus from Egypt.

The effect was large. One law now covered most people in the empire, and Roman law spread into local life in the provinces. Being a citizen no longer set a person apart. A new split, between the better off and the humble, took its place in the courts. The jurist Ulpian recorded the change in a single line later kept in the Digest.
sum: A law of 212 by the emperor Caracalla that made almost every free person in the Roman Empire a Roman citizen. Before it, full citizenship was held mainly by people in Italy, Roman colonies and some favoured towns and families.
